title: Ransomware leak-site post
description: A data-extortion group's leak-site entry as seen in Tor Browser: victim card with countdown timer to publication, data size, a short taunting description and a sample file tree. The group may be a real threat group; the victim is the exercising organization (simulated).

siteName.description: Leak blog name as shown in its header

onionUrl.description: Onion address in the address bar (invent one; 56 characters before .onion)

victimName.description: Victim organization name as the group writes it

sector.description: Sector label the group gives the victim

revenue.description: Revenue the group claims for the victim

dataSize.description: Size of the stolen data the group claims

countdown.description: Countdown timer frozen at the moment of the screenshot

status.description: countdown = timer running, published = data released (download links), negotiating = listing paused

description.description: The group's text about the victim (broken English is typical)
examples: Riverbend Regional Medical Center ignored us. We have patient records, HR files, financial documents. If no contact the data will be published.

fileList.description: Sample of the stolen file tree (up to 8 entries)

name.description: File or folder path (end folders with /)
